host: The IP address or hostname your server will bind to (e.g. "127.0.0.1" for localhost).
port: The TCP port number on which the server listens for incoming connections (e.g. 8888).
version: The version of the server implementation (e.g. "python", "rust")

logger.log_level: Specifies the minimum level of messages to record (e.g. "DEBUG" < "INFO" < "WARNING" < "ERROR" < "CRITICAL").
logger.enable_console_log: If true, log messages will be written to the console (stdout) using the console log format.
logger.console_log_format: Template for formatting console log messages, including ANSI escape codes for coloring (e.g. "\\033[92m%(asctime)s\\033[0m - \\033[94m%(name)s\\033[0m - %(levelname)s - %(message)s").
logger.enable_file_log: If true, log messages will be written to rotating log files on disk.
logger.enable_json_log: If true, file log entries will be emitted as JSON objects for structured logging.
logger.log_file_path: Filesystem directory where log files will be created and rotated.
logger.log_format: String template defining how file log messages are formatted (e.g. "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s").
logger.max_file_size: Maximum size in bytes of a single log file before it is rotated.
logger.backup_count: Number of rotated log files to retain before older logs are discarded.
logger.date_format: Format string for timestamps in log entries (e.g. "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f").
logger.log_keys: List of payload fields to include in JSON log files; use null for full payload, [] for no payload, or list specific field names to include.

hyper_parameters.connection_buffer_size: How many inbound connection attempts the OS will queue before refusing new ones. Higher values handle traffic spikes better (default 128).
hyper_parameters.command_buffer_size: Capacity of the channel holding backpressure commands before older commands are dropped (default 32).
hyper_parameters.control_channel_capacity: Buffer size for each client's control commands (throttle/flow-control) (default 8).
hyper_parameters.queue_monitor_capacity: How many backlog-size reports each client can queue before new reports are dropped (default 100).
hyper_parameters.client_timeout_secs: Seconds of client inactivity before the server forcibly disconnects them (default 300s). Set this to `null` or omit the field to disable timeouts and allow idle clients indefinitely.
hyper_parameters.rate_limit_msgs_per_minute: Maximum messages a client may send per minute before being throttled (default 300).
hyper_parameters.timeout_check_interval_secs: How often (in seconds) the server checks all clients for inactivity (default 30s).
hyper_parameters.accept_error_backoff_ms: Milliseconds to wait before retrying `accept()` after an error, to avoid tight loops (default 100ms).
hyper_parameters.quarantine_cooldown_secs: Seconds a client remains in quarantine after a forced disconnect (default 300s).
hyper_parameters.quarantine_cleanup_interval_secs: Seconds between automatic sweeps to remove expired quarantined clients (default 60s).
hyper_parameters.throttle_delay_ms: Delay (in milliseconds) applied when a client is throttled, to slow down message processing (default 200ms).
hyper_parameters.flow_control_delay_ms: Delay (in milliseconds) applied when flow control is active, pausing message handling (default 1000ms).
hyper_parameters.worker_threads: Number of Tokio runtime worker threads to spawn. Default is (number of CPU cores minus one).

backpressure_policy.enable_throttle: Turn on/off injecting delays when a client exceeds the throttle threshold.
backpressure_policy.throttle_threshold: Number of queued messages before throttling starts (default 100).
backpressure_policy.enable_flow_control: Turn on/off pausing reads when queue size exceeds the flow-control threshold.
backpressure_policy.flow_control_threshold: Number of queued messages before flow control starts (default 300).
backpressure_policy.enable_disconnect: Turn on/off forcefully disconnecting clients under extreme backlog.
backpressure_policy.disconnect_threshold: Number of queued messages before a client is disconnected (default 500).

dedicated_relay.enabled: If true, require identity-verified directed relay instead of legacy broadcast routing.
dedicated_relay.validation_adapter: Payload validation format to use. Currently supported: "aurora".
dedicated_relay.max_frame_bytes: Maximum newline-delimited payload size accepted by dedicated relay validation before rejection.
dedicated_relay.allowed_fingerprints: List of identity fingerprints allowed to access the server. Payloads from identities outside this list are rejected.
dedicated_relay.communication_graph: Directed adjacency map of sender fingerprint to allowed receiver fingerprints, used to prevent unrestricted broadcasting.

paths.envelope_root: Optional dot path to the signed relay envelope inside each payload. Use an empty string when the envelope is the payload root.
paths.sender_identity: Dot path, relative to the envelope root, where the sender identity object is found (for example "from").
paths.receiver_identity: Dot path, relative to the envelope root, where the receiver identity or receiver fingerprint is found (for example "to").
paths.envelope_signature: Dot path, relative to the envelope root, where the sender's envelope signature is found.
paths.sender_signing_key: Dot path, relative to the envelope root, where the sender identity's public signing key is found.
paths.sender_identity_signature: Dot path, relative to the envelope root, where the sender identity self-signature is found.

policy.allow_receiverless_binding: Allow a valid signed payload without a receiver to bind the connection to the sender identity.
policy.route_receiverless_to_graph: If true, receiverless valid payloads are relayed only to receivers listed for the sender in the communication graph.
policy.reject_unknown_receiver: If true, reject payloads addressed to receivers that are not in the allowed fingerprint list.
policy.reject_when_receiver_disconnected: If true, reject valid directed payloads when no connected client is currently bound to the receiver fingerprint.

invalid_attempts.enabled: If true, track repeated invalid dedicated relay attempts by remote IP and apply backpressure.
invalid_attempts.window_secs: Rolling time window in seconds used when counting invalid relay attempts.
invalid_attempts.max_entries: Maximum number of remote IP entries retained in the invalid-attempt tracker.
invalid_attempts.throttle_threshold: Invalid attempts within the window before throttle delay is applied.
invalid_attempts.flow_control_threshold: Invalid attempts within the window before flow-control delay is applied.
invalid_attempts.disconnect_threshold: Invalid attempts within the window before the connection is closed.
invalid_attempts.quarantine_threshold: Invalid attempts within the window before the remote IP is quarantined.
